title: Clock-Injected Time Map
prompt:
Implement `FrozenClock(initial=0)`, `TimeMap(clock)`, and `MonotonicTimeMap(clock)`. `FrozenClock.now()` returns its current value and `set(value)` changes it without sleeping. `TimeMap.set(key, value, timestamp=None)` uses the injected clock when timestamp is omitted and returns the assigned timestamp. `get(key, timestamp=None)` returns the value at the greatest stored timestamp less than or equal to the query, or `''` when none exists; an omitted query timestamp uses the injected clock.

Accept out-of-order numeric timestamps. A later write at the same timestamp wins, independent of value ordering. `MonotonicTimeMap.set` without an explicit timestamp assigns a strictly increasing timestamp even if its clock moves backward. Protect state for concurrent readers/writers without calling wall-clock time directly.

example.reasoning: Injected time makes temporal behavior deterministic and testable.
